evidence.why: ASSERTREPORT returns -1 on failure; the function validates the handle and returns free-cell payload capacity on success.

facts.rationale: Adds the explicit failure sentinel missing from the existing return-domain explanation while preserving the supported signature and success calculation.
facts.value: Signature: `long OSCheckHeap(int heap)`. The integer handle selects an active HeapArray descriptor in [0, NumHeaps). On successful validation, the return value is the sum of free-cell byte sizes minus HEADERSIZE for each free cell. If any ASSERTREPORT condition fails, the function reports the failed condition and returns -1 instead of a capacity.

evidence.why: Three assertion calls precede separate global read and write operations; no synchronization is present.

facts.rationale: Removes the unsupported atomic-exchange claim and distinguishes assertion preconditions from guaranteed runtime rejection.
facts.value: The function asserts allocator initialization, an in-range handle, and a nonnegative descriptor size, then separately reads __OSCurrHeap into prev, writes the requested heap handle, and returns prev. These are asserted preconditions, not an unconditional invalid-input rejection contract. The routine contains no synchronization establishing an atomic read-modify-write exchange.
